title_en: Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Railway Bureau — dispute over property rights protection
ruling_gist_en: 1. If a construction unit reaches a compensation intention with a mining rights holder for overlaying mineral resources and fulfills the approval procedures for such overlaying in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, then its act of overlaying mineral resources is not illegal, nor does it have subjective fault, and does not constitute infringement. The losses suffered by the mining rights holder due to the overlaying of mineral resources may be compensated in accordance with the law.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over protection of property rights; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Hebei Province; Beijing City; Legal person; Civil Code; Mineral Resources Law; Whether overlaying mineral resources constitutes infringement; Scope and standards of compensation; Determination of proper defendant; Partial support; Overlaying mineral resources; Railway construction; Loss of prospecting rights; Asset losses; Losses from cessation of production and business; Property rights; Jurisdiction; Dispute over protection of property rights with Beijing Railway Bureau
full_text_en:
Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Railway Bureau  
— Dispute over Property Rights Protection  

【Ruling Summary】  

1. Where a construction entity reaches an intention to compensate for mineral resource coverage with a mining right holder and has gone through the procedures for examination and approval of coverage in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, its act of covering the mineral resources is not illegal, and there is no subjective fault, thus it does not constitute infringement. The losses suffered by the mining right holder due to the coverage of the minerals may be compensated in accordance with the law.  

2. Where a construction project covers minerals for the public interest, the construction entity shall compensate the mining right holder for the amount payable for the covered resource reserves under market conditions at the time of coverage, as well as direct losses such as the exploration investment apportioned to the covered mining area, investment in existing mining facilities, and relocation of corresponding facilities.  

Supreme People's Court  
Civil Judgment  

(2017) Sup. People's Ct. Final No. 724  

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. Domicile: Change Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning Manchu Autonomous County, Hebei Province.  

Legal Representative: Ding Lianmao, Chairman of the Board.  

Authorized Litigation Agents: Yue Yunsheng, lawyer of Beijing Yuecheng Law Firm; Zhang Zhiwei, lawyer of Beijing Yuecheng Law Firm.  

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Railway Bureau. Domicile: No. 6, Fuxing Road, Haidian District, Beijing.  

Legal Representative: Guo Zhuxue, Director of the Bureau.  

Authorized Litigation Agents: Shi Zhezhi, lawyer of Tianjin Tianyuan Shitong Law Firm; Wang Dongmei, lawyer of Tianjin Tianyuan Shitong Law Firm.  

On August 1, 2014, the appellant Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Change Mining Company) filed a lawsuit with the Hebei High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) against the appellant Beijing Railway Bureau over a dispute concerning the protection of property rights. Beijing Railway Bureau raised an objection to jurisdiction. The court of first instance rendered a civil ruling on October 10, 2014 [(2014) Ji Li Min Chu Zi No. 9], rejecting the objection to jurisdiction raised by Beijing Railway Bureau. Beijing Railway Bureau, dissatisfied with that ruling, appealed. This Court rendered a civil ruling on March 20, 2015 [(2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 64], dismissing the appeal. The court of first instance rendered a civil judgment on June 27, 2017 [(2014) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 9]. Both parties, dissatisfied, appealed to this Court. After filing on September 13, 2017, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law and, pursuant to Article 134 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, held an in camera hearing of this case. The authorized litigation agents of the appellant Change Mining Company, Yue Yunsheng and Zhang Zhiwei, and the authorized litigation agents of the appellant Beijing Railway Bureau, Shi Zhezhi and Wang Dongmei, appeared in court. This case is now concluded.  

Change Mining Company's appeal requests: 1. To amend the judgment to add on the basis of Item 1 of the first-instance judgment an award of RMB 3,407,800 (exploration right loss of RMB 76,637,300 + asset loss of RMB 3,407,800 + operating expense loss during suspension of production of RMB 3,012,035 - RMB 5,000,000 already paid by Beijing Railway Bureau - RMB 74,649,335 awarded in the first-instance judgment) and interest loss (calculated on the base amount of RMB 78,057,135 at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, from May 9, 2011, until the date of actual full payment); 2. That Beijing Railway Bureau bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and Reasons: 1. The first-instance judgment erred in finding that Beijing Railway Bureau did not constitute infringement. Beijing Railway Bureau did not reach an agreement on compensation for covered mineral resources with Change Mining Company; the "Investigation and Assessment Report on the Coverage of Mineral Resources by the Land Used for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project" (hereinafter referred to as the "Investigation and Assessment Report") did not comply with mandatory provisions of laws and regulations; and the procedures applied by Beijing Railway Bureau for approval of coverage of mineral resources were not lawful. Beijing Railway Bureau has constituted infringement and shall bear liability for compensation. 2. As to the loss of exploration right, the assessment institution's taking of low values for factors such as mineral product prices and discount rate resulted in an undervaluation in the "Assessment Report on the Exploration Right for the Iron Ore General Survey at Lishugou, Change Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province." However, in order to resolve the dispute as soon as possible and avoid further expansion of losses, Change Mining Company will not appeal on this part. 3. As to asset loss, although the "Asset Appraisal Report on the Dispute between Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau over Property Rights Protection" [Ji Li Xin Ping Bao Zi (2016) No. 8066] (hereinafter referred to as the "No. 8066 Asset Appraisal Report") undervalues, Beijing Railway Bureau should at least compensate Change Mining Company for asset loss of RMB 3,407,800 based on this report. The first-instance judgment's use of the "Supplementary Report to the Asset Appraisal Report on the Dispute between Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau over Property Rights Protection [Ji Li Xin Ping Bao Zi (2016) No. 8066]" (hereinafter referred to as the "No. 8066 Asset Appraisal Supplementary Report"), calculated based on the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Registration Form for Expropriation and Occupation of Factory, Mine, Enterprise, and Institution Assets," as the basis for compensation is erroneous. 4. As to loss from suspension of production, although the valuation in the "Appraisal Report on the Dispute between Plaintiff Change Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau over Property Rights Protection" is low and does not include interest on borrowed funds invested by Change Mining Company in the iron ore project in question, Beijing Railway Bureau should at least compensate Change Mining Company for loss from suspension of production of RMB 3,012,035 based on this report. The first-instance judgment's use of the "Supplementary Explanation to the Appraisal Report on the Dispute between Plaintiff Fengning Change Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau over Property Rights Protection," prepared in accordance with the "Zhang-Tang Railway Chengde Section Land Expropriation and Demolition Method," as the basis for compensation is erroneous. Change Mining Company only acknowledges that the "Zhang-Tang Railway Chengde Section Land Expropriation and Demolition Method" is one of Beijing Railway Bureau's compensation policies and does not recognize that Beijing Railway Bureau has only used this method for compensation. Additionally, since the first-instance judgment already recognized the "Meeting Minutes" as legally valid, pursuant to paragraph 1(4) of the "Meeting Minutes," Change Mining Company entrusted an assessment institution to assess the losses caused by the coverage of mineral resources, and the assessment fees should be borne by Beijing Railway Bureau. 5. As to other reasonable economic losses, the first-instance judgment's discretionary award of interest starting from the date Change Mining Company filed the lawsuit lacks legal basis. On May 9, 2011, Beijing Railway Bureau formally notified Change Mining Company to cease operations. At that time, it should have compensated Change Mining Company for all losses in a lump sum, and interest should be calculated from that date. Subsequently, during the second-instance hearing of this Court, Change Mining Company amended its appeal requests orally to: 1. Amend the judgment to add on the basis of Item 1 of the first-instance judgment an award for interest loss to Change Mining Company, temporarily calculated to November 30, 2017, with the additional amount being RMB 16,800,143.89 (calculated on the base amount of RMB 74,649,335 already awarded in the first-instance judgment at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, from May 9, 2011, until the date of actual full payment, minus the interest of RMB 12,953,629.53 already supported in the first-instance judgment); 2. That Beijing Railway Bureau bear all litigation costs of this case.  

Beijing Railway Bureau argues: 1. The Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (hereinafter referred to as the Zhang-Tang Railway) project obtained the administrative authority's approval for coverage of mineral resources, with complete procedures, lawful and compliant. The first-instance judgment correctly found that Beijing Railway Bureau did not constitute infringement. 2. Change Mining Company acquired the mining right gratuitously, and its claim for loss of exploration right should not be supported. 3. Change Mining Company only held an exploration right, not a mining right, and therefore did not have the right to exploit, utilize, and obtain mineral resources. Thus, its claims for asset loss and loss from suspension of production should not be supported. 4. This case is a dispute over the protection of possession of property rights, and the reason Change Mining Company has not yet received compensation is not caused by Beijing Railway Bureau, but by Change Mining Company's failure to accept the compensation amount and reach a compensation agreement with the Chengde Railway Engineering Construction Command (hereinafter referred to as Chengdu Railway Command). Therefore, its claim for interest should not be supported. In summary, Change Mining Company's appeal lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.  

Beijing Railway Bureau's appeal requests: 1. To revoke the first-instance judgment and amend it to dismiss all of Change Mining Company's claims; 2. That Change Mining Company bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and Reasons: 1. Beijing Railway Bureau is not a proper defendant in this case. The court of first instance has already determined that this case is a dispute over compensation for expropriation and requisition, and Beijing Railway Bureau does not constitute infringement. Beijing Railway Bureau and Change Mining Company did not reach any compensation agreement, and the dispute between the parties is not a contractual dispute. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau cannot be regarded as a proper defendant based on an agency relationship. Mengji Railway Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mengji Company), as the investment construction unit, asset owner, asset beneficiary, and ultimate bearer of compensation costs for coverage of mineral resources for the Zhang-Tang Railway project, should bear compensation liability to Change Mining Company. 2. Loss of exploration right should not be compensated. Change Mining Company has not paid the exploration right use fees and exploration right prices for the Lishugou iron ore mine in question to the state, having acquired the exploration right gratuitously, and therefore compensation should not be awarded. Even if compensation is due, it should be based on the appraisal report issued by Hebei Lande Mining Right Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd. The court of first instance cannot simply treat the appraisal opinion issued by Hebei Mining Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd., commissioned by the court, as the basis for the judgment merely because the parties failed to successfully negotiate compensation for the exploration right. Moreover, the discounted cash flow method is not applicable to compensation for the coverage of mineral resources in this case. 3. Asset loss should not be compensated. Change Mining Company only holds an exploration right over the Lishugou iron ore mine, not a mining right. Assets such as the beneficiation plant and tailings pond have no necessary connection with exploration work. Moreover, the beneficiation plant and tailings pond are 6 kilometers away from the Lishugou iron ore mine, neither within the land expropriation and demolition scope of the Zhang-Tang Railway project nor within Change Mining Company's exploration area, and therefore are not subject to land expropriation and demolition. Change Mining Company is also not the legal owner of assets such as the beneficiation plant and tailings pond. The court of first instance cannot, based solely on the "Meeting Minutes" signed by Fengning Local Railway Construction and Demolition Office (hereinafter referred to as Fengning Demolition Office) and Change Mining Company and the "Asset Appraisal Report" issued by Chengde Yanfeng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd., determine that Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate for losses related to the beneficiation plant, tailings pond, and other assets. 4. The construction of the Zhang-Tang Railway project does not necessarily cause the beneficiation plant and tailings pond that Change Mining Company claims to be unable to operate, and therefore loss from suspension of production should not be compensated. 5. Interest loss should not be compensated. After this case was filed on August 1, 2014, Fengning Demolition Office, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations and based on the assessment results of the coverage scope extending 360 meters on each side of the railway centerline of the Zhang-Tang Railway project, paid Change Mining Company the full compensation amount of RMB 5 million. On January 7, 2015, the General Office of the Hebei Provincial People's Government issued the "Notice on the Work of Assessment and Compensation for Coverage of Minerals by the Zhang-Tang Railway," which caused the scope of coverage of mineral resources by the Zhang-Tang Railway project to expand and compensation costs to increase significantly. This was not the unilateral fault of Beijing Railway Bureau but resulted from the failure of the parties to reach consensus on the scope and amount of compensation. The corresponding interest should not be borne by Beijing Railway Bureau. The court of first instance's judgment ordering Beijing Railway Bureau to pay interest to Change Mining Company from August 1, 2014, lacks legal basis. In summary, the dispute in this case falls within the scope of compensation, not tort damages, and certainly not a contractual dispute. Beijing Railway Bureau, as the agent construction unit for the Zhang-Tang Railway project, should not bear compensation liability to Change Mining Company. This case should be handled in accordance with the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and the "Notice on Further Improving the Examination, Approval, and Management of Construction Projects Covering Important Mineral Resources" issued by the Ministry of Land and Resources (No. 137 [2010] of the Ministry of Land and Resources) (hereinafter referred to as Ministry of Land and Resources Document No. 137), to compensate Change Mining Company for actual losses such as the amount payable for the covered mineral resources under current market conditions, rather than compensat[ing] for losses including expected interests, such as the market value of the exploration right, based on a market transaction valuation method. The Zhang-Tang Railway project, as a national key railway construction project approved by the former National Development and Reform Commission, follows the same laws and regulations and uses the same valuation methods in the process of assessing compensation for coverage of mineral resources as other railway projects in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and even nationwide. If this case compensates for exploration right losses based on the market value assessment of mining rights, it will inevitably cause unrest and protest among mining rights holders who have already been compensated in the Zhang-Tang Railway project, and may even create a broad negative demonstration effect with serious social impact.  

Change Mining Company argues: 1. Change Mining Company is the lawful exploration right holder of the iron ore mine in question and enjoys the right to possess, use, and benefit from the iron ore mine. The Zhang-Tang Railway has been constructed and is in operation. Beijing Railway Bureau has objectively covered the iron ore mine in question and infringed on Change Mining Company's exploration right. The first-instance judgment correctly confirmed that Beijing Railway Bureau is the proper defendant in this case. 2. The court of first instance lawfully commissioned professional institutions to assess the loss of exploration right, asset loss, and loss from suspension of production. Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate according to the items and amounts determined in the first-instance judgment. 3. The time when Beijing Railway Bureau required Change Mining Company to cease operations was May 9, 2011. Beijing Railway Bureau should pay interest from that date. 4. Property rights of non-state-owned enterprises should also be equally and fairly protected. In summary, Beijing Railway Bureau's appeal is unfounded and should be dismissed.  

Change Mining Company's claims in the court of first instance: 1. To order Beijing Railway Bureau to compensate Change Mining Company for: loss of exploration right of RMB 115,913,500; loss of operating expenses during the period of suspension of production of RMB 31,620,413 (after deducting RMB 3,000,000 paid by Beijing Railway Bureau on September 5, 2014, and RMB 2,000,000 paid on October 11, 2014); loss of beneficiation plant assets of RMB 5,288,258; costs for closing the tailings pond of RMB 8,000,000; loss for road construction of RMB 2,000,000; and other reasonable economic losses (interest calculated on the principal amount of RMB 123,201,758 comprising loss of exploration right, asset loss, and road construction loss, at the loan interest rate of the bank for the corresponding period, from May 9, 2011, until the date of full payment). The above four items total RMB 200,001,000. 2. To order Beijing Railway Bureau to bear all litigation costs of this case.  

The court of first instance found the following facts:  

1. Facts concerning whether Beijing Railway Bureau is the proper defendant in this case. On October 30, 2010, Mengji Company, as the commissioning party, and Beijing Railway Bureau entered into an "Agreement on Authorized Construction Agency for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway," commissioning the entirety of construction management for the new Zhang-Tang Railway. On November 10, 2010, the Staffing Commission of Beijing Railway Bureau issued a "Notice on the Establishment of the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Engineering Construction Command," thereby establishing the Beijing Railway Bureau Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Engineering Construction Command (hereinafter referred to as Zhang-Tang Command), which was specifically responsible for the construction management of the Zhang-Tang Railway project. On February 5, 2013, and September 1, 2014, Zhang-Tang Command and the Chengde Railway Command entered into the "Agreement on Implementation of Compensation for Coverage of Minerals for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Chengde Section) Project" and the "Framework Agreement on Land Expropriation and Demolition for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Chengde Section) Project (IV)," stipulating that Zhang-Tang Command entrusted Chengde Railway Command to specifically carry out the assessment and compensation work for coverage of minerals in the Chengde area for the Zhang-Tang Railway project. During the implementation of the demolition and compensation work for the Zhang-Tang Railway project, Fengning Demolition Office, subordinate to Chengde Railway Command, conducted consultations with Change Mining Company regarding compensation for coverage of the Lishugou iron ore mine and, on May 27, 2014, produced "Meeting Minutes" confirming the fact of coverage recognized by both parties, the undisputed compensation items, and the main differences. On September 4, 2014, Fengning Demolition Office and Change Mining Company entered into an "Agreement," stipulating that Fengning Demolition Office would, on behalf of Beijing Railway Bureau, advance compensation for coverage of mineral resources in the amount of RMB 5,000,000, with the difference to be settled based on the court's judgment. This RMB 5,000,000 compensation has been actually paid. Additionally, during the project construction, Beijing Railway Bureau sent a letter to the Chengde Municipal People's Government reflecting the main issues encountered in the demolition work for the Zhang-Tang Railway project and requesting assistance.  

2. Facts concerning whether Beijing Railway Bureau committed infringing acts. On September 9, 2009, the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued a "Review Opinion" (Ji Guo Tu Zi Chu Ping [2009] No. 119) on the "Investigation and Assessment Report" submitted by Mengji Company, concluding that it agreed the report should pass review and could serve as the basis for applying for approval of coverage of mineral resources for the construction project. On September 23, 2009, the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued a "Reply on the Coverage of Mineral Resources by the 'New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project'" to Mengji Company's application for coverage of mineral resources by the land used for the Zhang-Tang Railway, approving, within the scope of the construction project, the coverage of proven important minerals: coal (2S21) 708,800 tons, iron ore (121B) 147,600 tons, copper (metal content) (333) 1,979 tons, and some building and non-metallic minerals. It recommended that the construction entity handle the compensation relationship with the mining rights holders and, as required, register the reserves of the covered mineral resources. Because the parties had major differences on issues such as the scope of assessment of exploration right loss and the scope of compensation for exploration rights, they were unable to sign a formal compensation agreement for coverage, giving rise to this litigation.

3. Facts regarding the items subject to compensation (compensation). On June 3, 2013, the Fengning Demolition Office submitted to the Chengde Railway Command the "Report on Compensation for Fengning Jiyuan Mining Co., Ltd. and Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. Beneficiation Plant," which stated: "Changge Mining Company was approved by the Fengning Manchu Autonomous County Economic and Trade Bureau in 2003 to invest RMB 5 million in the construction of an ore dressing plant. In 2009, Changge Mining Company had already met the conditions for converting exploration rights into mining rights. During the conversion process, the procedures were forced to terminate due to overlap with the construction of the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway. It is recommended that the construction entity respect the facts and provide reasonable compensation for the assets of the beneficiation plant." On June 28, 2013, witnessed and signed by representatives from the project headquarters, county headquarters, township governments, village committees, property owners, construction entities, design entities, construction entities, supervision entities, and on-site registrants (a total of ten parties), the assets of the Changge Mining Company's beneficiation plant were inventoried and registered, forming the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Asset Registration Form for Occupied Factory and Mining Enterprises and Institutions." According to the "Meeting Minutes" signed on May 27, 2014, between the Fengning Demolition Office and Changge Mining Company, the items of compensation agreed upon by both parties included the value of exploration rights, fixed asset investments, losses from the construction and closure of tailings ponds, and losses from production suspension and business cessation (the specific amount of compensation to be determined by an appraisal report issued by an appraisal institution with corresponding appraisal qualifications). The disagreements were: first, the scope of the appraisal of exploration right losses — whether it should be within 360 meters of the railway centerline or the entire overlapped mining area; second, the standard for appraising the value of exploration rights — whether to apply Document No. 137 of the Ministry of Land and Resources or the "China Mining Rights Appraisal Standards." Additionally, regarding the first point of disagreement, during litigation, Beijing Railway Bureau stated that, due to the issuance of the "Notice on the Appraisal and Compensation Work for Overlap of the Zhangtang Railway Mineral Resources" by the General Office of the Hebei Provincial People's Government in 2015, it agreed to the assessment scope of 1,000 meters from the railway centerline as claimed by Changge Mining Company. On April 10, 2014, Chengde Yanfeng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd., upon the entrustment of the Chengde Railway Command, issued the "Asset Appraisal Report" regarding the fair value of the assets of Changge Mining Company's beneficiation plant. The conclusion was that, as of the base date of January 6, 2011, the value of Changge Mining Company's demolished assets was RMB 1,983,100. After the lawsuit in this case was initiated on August 1, 2014, Changge Mining Company claimed that due to the overlap of the exploration rights, the tort losses that Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate included losses from exploration rights, asset losses, and losses from production suspension and business cessation. Beijing Railway Bureau, on the other hand, claimed that it had not committed any tortious act, and even if it were liable, it should be a compensation obligation arising from the national requisition of the exploration rights. At the same time, since what Changge Mining Company held was an exploration right, and what was actually overlapped was only the mining area of the exploration right, the compensation items should only involve compensation for the loss of exploration rights. On September 3, 2014, the Fengning Demolition Office issued the "Meeting Minutes," the main content of which was that due to the obstruction incident by Changge Mining Company, it was decided to advance RMB 5 million in compensation for Changge Mining Company's Lishugou Iron Mine (including RMB 4 million for production losses and RMB 1 million for certification fees and appraisal fees), with the final compensation amount to be determined by the court's judgment, and any surplus or deficiency to be settled accordingly.

4. Facts regarding the amount of compensation (compensation) for losses from exploration rights. On December 30, 2012, Hebei Lande Mining Rights Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd., upon the entrustment of the Chengde Railway Command, with the base date of January 16, 2011, and with reference to the price calculation method in the "Hebei Province Mining Rights Price Payment Measures (Trial)," issued the "Appraisal Consulting Report on the Prospecting Exploration Right of the Lishugou Iron Mine in Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province." The conclusion was that the value of the exploration right in question was RMB 19,267,200, and the preliminary exploration investment was RMB 4,816,800 (determined at 20% of the mining right price). During litigation, Beijing Railway Bureau consistently insisted that this appraisal report (or a judicial appraisal opinion made using the appraisal method of that report) should be the basis for the compensation amount. On May 15, 2013, entrusted by Changge Mining Company, Beijing Yuehaixinyuan Mining Consulting Co., Ltd., with the base date of April 30, 2013, using the discounted cash flow method, issued the "Appraisal Consulting Report on the Prospecting Exploration Right of the Lishugou Iron Mine in Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province (Railway Overlap and Affected Area)." The conclusion was that the value of the exploration right in question was RMB 115,913,500. During litigation, because the parties could not reach an agreement on this issue and did not mutually accept the unilateral appraisal conclusions made before the lawsuit, the court of first instance, upon the application of Changge Mining Company, entrusted Hebei Mining Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise the value of the exploration right in question (the original entrusted appraisal item was to appraise the compensation amount for overlapping of exploration rights, but the appraisal entity stated that it could only appraise the value of the exploration right, so the entrusted appraisal item was modified). On December 14, 2016, Hebei Mining Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the "Appraisal Report on the Prospecting Exploration Right of the Lishugou Iron Mine in Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province," with the base date of January 16, 2011, using the discounted cash flow method, concluding the exploration right value at RMB 76,637,300. After this judicial appraisal opinion was served on both parties, both parties submitted written objections. Changge Mining Company's objections mainly focused on three issues: first, the sales price; second, the value of the discount rate; third, the value of the 9.0803 million ton overlapped area in the report's valuation. Beijing Railway Bureau raised three main objections: first, the appraisal should not have used the discounted cash flow method; second, the development and utilization plan submitted by Changge Mining Company could not be used as an appraisal basis; third, the iron ore sales price used in the appraisal was obviously too high, failing to consider the downward trend in the market since 2011. Hebei Mining Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. conducted a review of the appraisal in response to the written objections and issued a written objection response on March 15, 2017, which did not adopt the objections raised by either party. The appraisal entity appeared in court on March 16, 2017, to be examined.

5. Facts regarding the amount of compensation (compensation) for asset losses. Because the parties could not reach an agreement during litigation, the court of first instance, upon the application of Changge Mining Company, entrusted Hebei Lixin Anqiao Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise the asset losses claimed by Changge Mining Company. Based on the materials submitted by Changge Mining Company (Beijing Railway Bureau fundamentally denied this compensation item and therefore did not accept any materials submitted by Changge Mining Company), Hebei Lixin Anqiao Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the "8066 Asset Appraisal Report" on December 22, 2016. With the base date of January 16, 2011, and using the cost method, the appraisal concluded that the total appraised value of assets was RMB 3,407,800, including RMB 119,700 for road construction, RMB 2,648,100 for buildings, structures, equipment, and trees, and RMB 640,000 for the cost of closing the tailings pond. After the "8066 Asset Appraisal Report" was served on both parties, both parties submitted written objections. Changge Mining Company's main objection was that the appraised value was too low. Beijing Railway Bureau's main objection was that it did not accept this judicial appraisal item, and that the materials supporting the relevant losses were prepared and submitted unilaterally by Changge Mining Company and could not be used as a basis for appraisal. On March 10, 2017, Hebei Lixin Anqiao Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. responded to the written objections of both parties and did not adopt the objections raised by either party. The appraisal entity appeared in court on March 16, 2017, to be examined by both parties. Additionally, after the "8066 Asset Appraisal Report" was issued, the court of first instance, upon the application of Changge Mining Company, obtained evidence including the aforementioned "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Asset Registration Form for Occupied Factory and Mining Enterprises and Institutions." Because this registration form had been confirmed by multiple parties, the court of first instance instructed the appraisal entity to review the asset value of the beneficiation plant based on this registration form. On March 29, 2017, Hebei Lixin Anqiao Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the "8066 Asset Appraisal Supplemental Report," concluding that the appraised value of the assets recorded in the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Asset Registration Form for Occupied Factory and Mining Enterprises and Institutions" was RMB 1,491,900. This amount did not include the tree appraisal value of RMB 12,608, the additional increase for road extension of RMB 83,730, the site leveling fee of RMB 458,710, the tailings pond construction fee of RMB 718,130, and the tailings pond closure fee of RMB 640,000. After the "8066 Asset Appraisal Supplemental Report" was served on both parties, Changge Mining Company stated that its relevant objections would be those raised at the trial. Beijing Railway Bureau still fundamentally denied this appraisal item.

6. Facts regarding the amount of compensation (compensation) for losses from production suspension and business cessation. Upon the application of Changge Mining Company, the court of first instance entrusted Hebei Lixin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. to appraise the work stoppage losses claimed by Changge Mining Company. Based on the materials submitted by Changge Mining Company (Beijing Railway Bureau also fundamentally denied this compensation item and therefore did not accept any materials submitted by Changge Mining Company), Hebei Lixin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. issued the "Appraisal Report on the Property Rights Protection Dispute Case Between Plaintiff Changge Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau" on December 16, 2016. The conclusion was that during the period of production suspension and business cessation from May 9, 2011 to May 31, 2016, the total operating expenses were RMB 3,012,035.71. After this appraisal report was served on both parties, Changge Mining Company objected that the appraisal result was too low and did not calculate interest. Beijing Railway Bureau objected that this item should not be included in the scope of compensation, and that the materials relied upon were prepared and submitted unilaterally by Changge Mining Company. On March 16, 2017, Hebei Lixin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. appeared in court to be examined by both parties. During the trial, both parties acknowledged the legality and validity of the "Measures for Land Acquisition and Demolition for the Chengde Section of the Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway," issued by the Chengde Municipal People's Government on November 22, 2010. Article 20, paragraph 6 of those Measures stipulates that for commercial enterprises, the following additional expenses shall be provided: "(1) Where an enterprise suffers production suspension or business cessation due to the impact of relocation, compensation shall be calculated based on the actual number of employees of the enterprise and the average per capita wage of the six months prior to demolition in the district published by the statistical department of the demolition location, with the payment period being six months. The number of employees shall be based on the social insurance payment certificate provided by the social security department. (2) For losses caused by production suspension or business cessation during the relocation and construction process of a relocated enterprise, compensation shall be calculated based on the average profit of the six months prior to relocation, for a period of six months..." During litigation, Changge Mining Company stated that it had not carried out ore mining or actual operation because it had not completed the procedures for converting exploration rights into mining rights. The court of first instance instructed the appraisal entity to conduct a supplemental appraisal based on the compensation standards provided in the above measures, for reference in the court's judgment. On March 29, 2017, Hebei Lixin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. issued the "Appraisal Report on the Property Rights Protection Dispute Case Between Plaintiff Changge Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau (Supplemental Explanation)," calculating, based on data published by the Hebei Provincial Bureau of Statistics, a six-month wage for 10 employees of Changge Mining Company at RMB 162,005. Changge Mining Company expressed non-acceptance of this supplemental explanation, while Beijing Railway Bureau still fundamentally denied this compensation item as a whole.

The court of first instance held that the main issues in dispute in this case were three: first, whether Beijing Railway Bureau was the proper defendant in this case; second, whether Beijing Railway Bureau had engaged in a tortious act and whether it should bear liability for compensation or compensation; third, what items and corresponding amounts Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate (compensation) and how interest should be calculated.

Regarding the issue of whether Beijing Railway Bureau was the proper defendant in this case. Article 403, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "Where the agent fails to perform its obligations towards the third party due to the principal's reasons, the agent shall disclose the principal to the third party, and the third party may then choose either the agent or the principal as the counterparty to assert its rights, but the third party may not change the selected counterparty." In this case, according to the "Newly Built Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Entrusted Construction Agreement" signed between third-party Mengji Company (the client) and Beijing Railway Bureau, the construction entity for the Zhangtang Railway project involved in this case was Mengji Company, and Beijing Railway Bureau, as the agent, was responsible for all construction management work. A mandate relationship existed between the two. After accepting the mandate, Beijing Railway Bureau established the Zhangtang Project Department, which signed a framework agreement on overlapping compensation for the Chengde section with the Chengde Railway Command. The Fengning Demolition Office, a subordinate body of the Chengde Railway Command, then negotiated multiple times with Changge Mining Company regarding overlapping compensation in the name of Beijing Railway Bureau, signed written meeting minutes, and prepaid RMB 5 million in compensation in the name of Beijing Railway Bureau. Therefore, Changge Mining Company had the right to choose to assert its rights against either Beijing Railway Bureau or Mengji Company. After the lawsuit in this case was initiated, Beijing Railway Bureau disclosed its mandate relationship with Mengji Company and requested to add Mengji Company as a defendant in this case, but Changge Mining Company explicitly refused to agree to such addition. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau was the proper defendant in this case and should bear corresponding compensation or compensation liability.

Regarding the issue of whether Beijing Railway Bureau had engaged in a tortious act and whether it should bear liability for compensation or compensation. During the trial, Beijing Railway Bureau explicitly acknowledged that Changge Mining Company was the holder of the exploration right for the Lishugou Iron Mine and had standing as the plaintiff. According to Article 123 of the Property Law of the PRC, an exploration right is a usufructuary right and should be protected by law. The fact that the exploration right held by Changge Mining Company had been actually overlapped was confirmed in the "Meeting Minutes" of May 27, 2014. The core dispute between the parties was whether this overlapping act was lawful, i.e., whether Beijing Railway Bureau had committed a tort. Based on the facts found, on September 23, 2009, the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources had issued the "Reply on the Overlap of Mineral Resources by the 'Newly Built Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project'" in response to Mengji Company's application for overlapping mineral resources for the Zhangtang Railway construction land, approving the overlapping of mineral resources, including the exploration right in question, within the scope of the construction project. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau did not constitute a tort. Article 121 of the Property Law of the PRC provides: "Where a usufructuary right is extinguished or its exercise is affected due to the requisition or expropriation of immovable or movable property, the usufructuary right holder has the right to obtain corresponding compensation in accordance with Articles 42 and 44 of this Law." Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate Changge Mining Company for the economic losses caused by the overlapping of the exploration right.

Regarding the issue of the items for which Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate. Beijing Railway Bureau should bear compensation liability in accordance with the law. Regarding the items that should be compensated, during litigation, Beijing Railway Bureau agreed to compensate for the loss of exploration rights, which was confirmed by the court of first instance. As for the asset losses and losses from production suspension and business cessation claimed by Changge Mining Company, although the Zhangtang Railway only overlapped the mining area of the exploration right in question and did not directly overlap the beneficiation plant invested and constructed by Changge Mining Company, the exploration right in question was at the stage of handling the procedures for converting exploration rights into mining rights. Changge Mining Company's advance investment in constructing the supporting beneficiation plant was approved by the administrative department, and it had also obtained the safety production permit for the tailings pond. The inability to continue the procedures for converting exploration rights into mining rights directly led to the inability to directly operate the supporting beneficiation plant. Therefore, asset losses and losses from production suspension and business cessation should be included in the scope of compensation. At the same time, the "Meeting Minutes" signed between the Fengning Demolition Office and Changge Mining Company had explicitly agreed to compensate for the above two losses. Although Beijing Railway Bureau argued in litigation that the actions of the Fengning Demolition Office exceeded its authority and that it was unaware of and did not accept them, the Fengning Demolition Office was a subordinate body of the Chengde Railway Command, the Chengde Railway Command had signed an entrustment agreement with the Zhangtang Command, and the Zhangtang Command was established by Beijing Railway Bureau. Therefore, there should be close connections among the four parties in the daily work of demolition and compensation for the Zhangtang Railway. Beijing Railway Bureau's claim that it was unaware of the negotiations conducted by the Fengning Demolition Office, the reports submitted, and the entrustment by the Chengde Railway Command to Chengde Yanfeng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise the assets of the beneficiation plant was inconsistent with common sense. Moreover, the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Asset Registration Form for Occupied Factory and Mining Enterprises and Institutions" lawfully obtained by the court of first instance was witnessed and signed by ten parties, including representatives of the project headquarters, county headquarters, township governments, village committees, property owners, construction entities, design entities, construction entities, supervision entities, and on-site registrants. Therefore, the defense of Beijing Railway Bureau was not supported.

Regarding the amount of compensation for loss of exploration rights. According to the appraisal opinion made by Hebei Mining Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd., with the base date of January 16, 2011, and using the discounted cash flow method, the value of the exploration right in question was RMB 76,637,300. According to the appraisal report made by Hebei Lande Mining Rights Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd., entrusted by the Chengde Railway Command before the lawsuit, with the base date of January 16, 2011, and with reference to the price calculation method in the "Hebei Province Mining Rights Price Payment Measures (Trial)," the value of the exploration right in question was RMB 19,267,200, and the preliminary exploration investment was RMB 4,816,800 (determined at 20% of the mining right price). The two appraisal conclusions used the same base date and confirmed the same amount of overlapped mineral reserves. The only difference was the appraisal method. Regarding the standard of compensation for overlapping mineral resources, the Property Law of the PRC did not provide clear provisions. Article 4, paragraph 3 of Document No. 137 of the Ministry of Land and Resources provides: "Where a construction project overlaps mineral resources for which mining rights have already been established, the new land user shall also simultaneously sign an agreement with the mining right holder. The agreement shall include the mining right holder's consent to abandon the overlapped mining area scope and related compensation content. The scope of compensation shall, in principle, include: 1. The price that the mining right holder should pay for the overlapped resource reserves under current market conditions (excluding those obtained without payment); 2. Direct losses such as the exploration investment borne by the overlapped mineral resources, investment in existing mining facilities, and relocation of corresponding facilities." The above provision first emphasizes that the parties must negotiate and sign a specific compensation agreement, and the listed compensation scope is also "in principle, include," so it should be a guiding provision, not a mandatory one. Where the parties cannot reach an agreement through consultation, the appraisal opinion made by Hebei Mining Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd., which had lawful procedures and also complied with the principle of fairness, should be used as the basis for the decision.

Regarding the issue of asset losses. According to the "Supplemental Asset Appraisal Report No. 8066" issued by Hebei Lixin Anqiao Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. on March 29, 2017, the asset appraisal value recorded in the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Land Acquisition Asset Registration Form for Factories, Mines, Enterprises and Institutions" signed by ten parties was RMB 1,491,900 (this amount did not include the tree appraisal value of RMB 12,608, the road extension increase value of RMB 83,730, the site leveling fee of RMB 458,710, the tailings pond construction fee of RMB 718,130, and the tailings pond closure fee of RMB 640,000). Because the "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Land Acquisition Asset Registration Form for Factories, Mines, Enterprises and Institutions" is the original document verified and signed by all parties, it is more objective than the inspection materials submitted unilaterally by Changge Mining Company, and the "Supplemental Asset Appraisal Report No. 8066" should serve as the basis for final adjudication. The asset loss amount for the concentrator was RMB 1,491,900. In addition, according to the "Negotiation Minutes" signed by Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office and Changge Mining Company, the investment in tailings pond construction and closure costs were items eligible for compensation. Moreover, the tailings pond had obtained legal procedures, so the tailings pond construction fee of RMB 718,130 and the tailings pond closure fee of RMB 640,000 should be included in the scope of compensation. The total asset loss amount was RMB 2,850,030.

Regarding the amount of compensation for production and business suspension losses. During the trial, both parties acknowledged the legality and validity of the "Measures for Land Acquisition and Demolition for the Zhang-Tang Railway Chengde Section" issued by the Chengde Municipal People's Government on November 22, 2010. Pursuant to these Measures, Hebei Lixin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. issued a supplemental explanation on March 29, 2017. According to data published by the Hebei Provincial Bureau of Statistics, the half-year wages for ten employees of Changge Mining Company amounted to RMB 162,005, which should serve as the amount of compensation for Changge Mining Company's production and business suspension losses.

In summary, the total compensation amount that Beijing Railway Bureau should pay to Changge Mining Company for the mineral resources overlain was RMB 76,637,300 (exploration right loss) + RMB 2,850,030 (asset loss) + RMB 162,005 (production and business suspension loss) = RMB 79,649,335. Deducting the RMB 5 million already paid by Beijing Railway Bureau, an additional compensation of RMB 74,649,335 remained payable. Furthermore, from January 16, 2011, the date when the mineral resources were actually overlain, the parties had been unable to reach an agreement on the compensation standard. The court of first instance determined interest at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China, calculated from the date Changge Mining Company filed the lawsuit, i.e., August 1, 2014.

The court of first instance ruled: (1) Beijing Railway Bureau shall pay Changge Mining Company mineral resource overlain compensation of RMB 74,649,335 and interest (with interest calculated on the base amount of RMB 74,649,335 from August 1, 2014, until the date of actual full performance, at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China) within fifteen days after the judgment takes effect; (2) All other claims of Changge Mining Company were dismissed. Case acceptance fee of RMB 1,041,805 was to be borne by Changge Mining Company (RMB 591,805) and Beijing Railway Bureau (RMB 450,000); the appraisal fee of RMB 481,100 was to be borne equally by both parties.

During the second instance proceedings of this court, the parties submitted evidence in support of their appeals in accordance with the law. This court organized the parties for evidence exchange and cross-examination.

Beijing Railway Bureau submitted three sets of evidence as new evidence at the second instance hearing.

First set of evidence: five documents in total. Evidence 1 is the enterprise credit information public report of Changge Mining Company; Evidence 2 is the enterprise credit information public report of Beijing Oriental Tengda Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Tengda Company). Evidence 1 and 2 were obtained from the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, intended to prove that the legal representatives of both Changge Mining Company and Tengda Company were Ding Lianmao. Evidence 3 is the outer flyleaf of the appendix to the "Investigation and Evaluation Report"; Evidence 4 is the "Notice on Issuing Mineral Exploration Permit No. [2007] 0315" and its attached map (Registration Map of the Mineral Exploration Block for the Iron Ore General Survey at Lishugou, Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province); Evidence 5 is the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for the Overlaying of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway" signed by Meng-Ji Company and Tengda Company on August 8, 2009. Evidence 3, 4, and 5 were obtained from Meng-Ji Company, intended to prove that Meng-Ji Company's procedures for applying for the overlaying of mineral resources were complete and legal, and that Beijing Railway Bureau, as the construction agent for the Zhang-Tang Railway project, acted lawfully and compliantly in implementing the overlaying of mineral resources under the entrustment of Meng-Ji Company, and thus no infringement existed.

Second set of evidence: Evidence 6 is the information on the Lishugou Iron Ore General Survey project in Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province, from the exploration right registration information verification platform of the former Ministry of Land and Resources. This evidence was obtained from the official website of the former Ministry of Land and Resources before the second instance hearing, intended to prove that Changge Mining Company's exploration right was still lawfully subsisting, and that the Zhang-Tang Railway project had not overlain the mineral resources of the Lishugou iron ore involved in the case.

Third set of evidence: Evidence 7 is the information of Changge Mining Company in the national mining rights holder exploration and mining information publication system of the former Ministry of Land and Resources. This evidence was obtained from the official website of the former Ministry of Land and Resources before the second instance hearing, intended to prove that Changge Mining Company had obtained the exploration right involved in the case without consideration and therefore should not receive compensation.

Changge Mining Company's cross-examination stated: (1) The authenticity and legality of Evidence 1, 2, 4, and 5 were acknowledged, but their relevance was not. Evidence 3 was incomplete, having only an outer flyleaf, so its authenticity, legality, and relevance were all denied. The intended proof of this set of evidence was denied. The document between Tengda Company and Meng-Ji Company was merely a letter of intent for compensation, which did not specify core terms such as compensation items, amounts, or timing, and was not a true compensation agreement. The "Investigation and Evaluation Report" should have had a compensation agreement attached, not a letter of intent. Therefore, this set of evidence could not prove that the procedures for overlaying mineral resources were lawful, still less could it prove that Beijing Railway Bureau had not committed infringement. (2) The authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 6 were acknowledged, but its intended proof was denied. Beijing Railway Bureau had not provided lawful compensation to Changge Mining Company and did not meet the conditions required by the administrative authorities for registering the reserves of overlain mineral resources, so Changge Mining Company could continue to apply for the renewal of the exploration right. The Zhang-Tang Railway had already commenced operation, and the fact that the iron ore involved in the case had been overlain was objectively existing. (3) The authenticity and legality of the source of Evidence 7 were acknowledged, but the authenticity of some of the content recorded in this evidence was not acknowledged, and its intended proof was denied. Changge Mining Company had paid the exploration right usage fee to the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources on schedule.

This court holds: Evidence 1, 2, 4, and 5, given that Changge Mining Company acknowledged their authenticity and legality, may be admitted as evidence. Their intended proof must be determined in conjunction with other evidence and the facts of the case. Evidence 3, being only the outer flyleaf of the appendix to the "Investigation and Evaluation Report," does not meet the completeness requirement for evidence and is not admitted. Evidence 6 and 7, whose authenticity was acknowledged by Changge Mining Company, contain contradictions with the evidence submitted by Changge Mining Company during the first instance and need to be determined in conjunction with other evidence.

This court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This court additionally finds: At the end of 2015, the Zhang-Tang Railway was completed and officially commenced operation. Changge Mining Company went through the procedures for the renewal of the exploration right involved in the case, and the exploration right involved in the case remained registered in the name of Changge Mining Company.

This court holds that the issues in dispute in the second instance are: First, whether Beijing Railway Bureau is a proper defendant in this case; Second, whether Beijing Railway Bureau committed any tort and whether it should bear liability for compensation or liability for indemnity; Third, the items, amounts, and calculation of interest for which Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate or indemnify.

(I) Regarding the issue of whether Beijing Railway Bureau is a proper defendant in this case.

The investor and construction entity for the Zhang-Tang Railway project was Meng-Ji Company. Meng-Ji Company and Beijing Railway Bureau signed the "Agreement on Authorized Construction Agency for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway" stipulating that Meng-Ji Company entrusted Beijing Railway Bureau to be responsible for all construction management work of the Zhang-Tang Railway project, including the work related to land acquisition and demolition, mineral resource overlain compensation, etc., and to allocate other fees including project management fees. To perform the authorized construction agency agreement, Beijing Railway Bureau established the Zhang-Tang Command and authorized it to specifically implement all the work that Beijing Railway Bureau should undertake under the agreement. Subsequently, the Zhang-Tang Command signed the "Implementation Agreement on Mineral Overlaying Compensation for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Chengde Section) Project" and the "Framework Agreement on Land Acquisition and Demolition for the New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway (Chengde Section) Project (IV)" with the Chengde Municipal Railway Construction Headquarters, stipulating that the Zhang-Tang Command entrusted the Chengde Municipal Railway Construction Headquarters with the responsibility for specifically implementing the assessment and compensation work for overlain mineral resources in the Chengde area of the Zhang-Tang Railway project. Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office, as a subordinate unit of the Chengde Municipal Railway Construction Headquarters, was responsible for the assessment and compensation work for overlain mineral resources in Fengning County. In fact, before litigation, Changge Mining Company had been asserting to Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office for the assessment and compensation of overlain mineral resources, and Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office had also been negotiating with Changge Mining Company regarding the relevant compensation issues. During the second instance trial, Beijing Railway Bureau also acknowledged the mineral resource overlain compensation agreements signed by Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office and other mining rights holders. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau shall bear legal liability for the consequences of the mineral resource overlain compensation actions carried out by the implementing units within the scope of their delegated authority. Beijing Railway Bureau's argument that it is not a proper defendant in this case cannot be sustained, and this court does not support it.

(II) Regarding the issue of whether Beijing Railway Bureau committed any tort and whether it should bear liability for compensation or liability for indemnity.

Pursuant to Article 123 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the exploration right, mining right, water right, and the right to use water areas and tidal flats for breeding and fishing acquired lawfully shall be protected by law," the mining right lawfully obtained by Changge Mining Company is protected by law. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "a person who through fault infringes upon another person's civil rights and interests shall bear tort liability," Changge Mining Company, claiming that Beijing Railway Bureau constituted a tort, must prove that Beijing Railway Bureau was at fault in carrying out the act of overlaying mineral resources. According to the facts ascertained in this case, the "Letter of Intent for Compensation for the Overlaying of Mining Rights by the Proposed Zhang-Tang Railway" signed by Meng-Ji Company and Tengda Company on August 8, 2009, clearly stipulated: "To ensure the implementation of the national key project, the mining rights holder and the construction entity, through friendly consultation, agree to the overlaying of the mining rights. Both parties agree that after the project is formally established, a compensation agreement shall be signed through negotiation between both parties based on the assessment report on overlain mineral resources approved by the provincial department of land and resources, national policies, and relevant regulations." On September 23, 2009, the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued a "Reply on the Overlaying of Mineral Resources for the 'New Zhangjiakou-Tangshan Railway Construction Project'" in response to Meng-Ji Company's application for the overlaying of mineral resources for the Zhang-Tang Railway construction land, approving the overlaying of known important mineral resources within the scope of the construction project. Among the parties in this case, Beijing Railway Bureau accepted the entrustment from Meng-Ji Company to be responsible for the construction of the Zhang-Tang Railway project; Changge Mining Company acquired the mining right involved in the case by transfer from the non-party Tengda Company, and the legal representatives of both Changge Mining Company and Tengda Company were Ding Lianmao. After reaching the intent on overlaying compensation with Tengda Company, Meng-Ji Company went through the approval procedures for overlaying important mineral resources in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau's act of overlaying the exploration right registered under Changge Mining Company's name during the construction of the Zhang-Tang Railway project was not illegal, and there was no subjective fault; thus, it did not constitute a tort. Consequently, Changge Mining Company's argument that Beijing Railway Bureau constituted a tort cannot be sustained. The losses suffered by Changge Mining Company's exploration right due to the overlaying act by Beijing Railway Bureau shall be compensated as a matter of law.

(III) Regarding the issue of items, amounts, and interest for which Beijing Railway Bureau should compensate.

Regarding the items of compensation. First, the loss of the exploration right. During the first instance, Beijing Railway Bureau acknowledged that compensation should be made for the loss of the exploration right involved in the case, but on appeal, it argued that because Changge Mining Company had obtained the exploration right without consideration, compensation for the exploration right loss should not be granted. The former Ministry of Land and Resources' "Interim Measures for the Administration of Bidding, Auction, and Listing for the Transfer of Exploration Rights and Mining Rights" and the "Notice on Issues Concerning Deepening the Reform of the System for Obtaining Exploration Rights and Mining Rights for Valuable Consideration" jointly issued by the Ministry of Finance and the former Ministry of Land and Resources provide that the system of obtaining exploration rights for valuable consideration is to be fully implemented. According to the "Explanation on the Retention of the Exploration Right for the Iron Ore General Survey at Lishugou, Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province" issued by the Fengning Manchu Autonomous County Bureau of Land and Resources on May 25, 2015, the exploration right for the "General Survey of the Lishugou Iron Ore at Changge Village, Nanguan Township, Fengning County, Hebei Province" was obtained through listing in June 2005. Beijing Railway Bureau's assertion that Changge Mining Company obtained the exploration right without consideration and should not receive compensation is not supported by sufficient evidence, and this argument on appeal cannot be sustained. Second, asset losses and production and business suspension losses. Although the Zhang-Tang Railway only overlain the mining area of the exploration right involved in the case, the exploration right was already at the stage of processing the conversion from exploration to mining. Changge Mining Company had previously invested in constructing a supporting concentrator, which was approved by the administrative authorities, and also obtained a safety production license for the tailings pond. The inability to continue the procedures for conversion from exploration to mining directly resulted in the inability of the supporting concentrator to carry out production and business activities. Therefore, the asset loss and production and business suspension loss of the concentrator objectively existed. Moreover, the "Negotiation Minutes" signed by Fengning Demolition and Relocation Office and Changge Mining Company on May 21, 2014, had clearly acknowledged the above two losses. The "Zhang-Tang Railway (Chengde Section) Land Acquisition Asset Registration Form for Factories, Mines, Enterprises and Institutions" obtained by the court of first instance according to law bore the signatures and witness of representatives from ten parties, including the project headquarters, county headquarters, township government, village committee, property owner, construction entity, design entity, construction unit, supervision unit, and on-site recorder. Therefore, Beijing Railway Bureau's argument on appeal that it should not compensate for Changge Mining Company's asset losses and production and business suspension losses cannot be sustained.

Regarding the amount of compensation. The parties in this case no longer disputed that compensation should be made for the exploration right within 1,000 meters on both sides of the railway centerline and the amount of mineral resource reserves overlain. This court holds that the scope of compensation for overlain mineral resources should be limited to the price that the mining rights holder would need to pay for the overlain reserves under current market conditions, as well as direct losses such as the exploration investment attributable to the overlain mining area, the investment in existing mining facilities, and costs for relocating corresponding facilities. Particularly for an exploration right, whether it can be converted into a mining right remains uncertain; even if converted into a mining right, the exploration right holder would still need to pay the necessary usage fees to the state for the realization of the mining right and invest substantial amounts in construction and production operation costs; from the perspective of market risk, investing in a mining right also faces the risk of fluctuations in mineral product market prices, and the expected profits of the mining right holder may not be realized. For Changge Mining Company, which only owned an exploration right, compensation based on the aforementioned standards adequately protects its lawful rights and interests and is generally consistent with the compensation received by other mining rights holders who have reached compensation agreements. Hebei Lande Mining Rights Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd., entrusted by the Chengde Municipal Railway Construction Headquarters, assessed the value of the overlain mining right by reference to the price calculation method in the "Hebei Provincial Measures for the Payment of Mining Rights Prices (Trial)." Its conclusion is reasonable and can serve as the basis for determining the compensation amount. Accordingly, the value of the exploration right involved in the case was RMB 19,267,200, and the preliminary exploration investment was RMB 4,816,800. For asset losses and production and business suspension losses, the procedures for preparing the "Supplemental Asset Appraisal Report No. 8066" and the "Appraisal Report on the Right Protection Dispute Case between Plaintiff Changge Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau (Supplemental Explanation)" were lawful and well-founded, and this court admits them as evidence. Accordingly, Changge Mining Company's asset loss was RMB 2,850,030 and its production and business suspension loss was RMB 162,005.

The total amount of compensation that Beijing Railway Bureau shall pay to Changge Mining Company was RMB 19,267,200 (loss of exploration right) + RMB 4,816,800 (preliminary exploration investment) + RMB 2,850,030 (asset loss) + RMB 162,005 (production and business suspension loss) = RMB 27,096,035. Deducting the RMB 5 million already paid by Beijing Railway Bureau, an additional RMB 22,096,035 remained payable.

Regarding the issue of interest. Considering that the dispute over the exploration right in this case lasted for several years, and the parties could not reach an agreement on the compensation amount resulting in an inability to actually perform, for which both parties bore responsibility, it is reasonable to calculate interest from the date of filing this lawsuit, i.e., August 1, 2014, at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for loans of the same type.

In summary, Changge Mining Company's appeal claims cannot be sustained, and this court does not support them; Beijing Railway Bureau's appeal claims are partially sustained, and this court supports the sustained part. Pursuant to Item 2 of Article 170, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2014) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 9 of the Hebei High People's Court is reversed;

2. Beijing Railway Bureau shall pay Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. compensation of RMB 22,096,035 within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect (with interest calculated on the base amount of RMB 22,096,035 at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for loans of the same type from August 1, 2014, until the date of actual full performance);

3. All other claims of Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the amount of debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

First instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,041,805 shall be borne by Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. (RMB 885,535) and Beijing Railway Bureau (RMB 156,270); appraisal fee of RMB 481,100 shall be borne equally by Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. and Beijing Railway Bureau. Second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,075,867.4 shall be borne by Fengning Changge Mining Co., Ltd. (RMB 1,050,867.4) and Beijing Railway Bureau (RMB 25,000).

This judgment is final.
